title: Stock Market Highlights, Sept 8: Sensex down 555 pts, Nifty ends at 23,635 as crude oil nears $100 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights - Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 8th September 2026.

On Tuesday, Sensex dropped 555.23 points or -0.73% to 75,577.58, while Nifty 50 down 144.05 points (-0.61%) to close at 23,635.10. The closing auction session (CAS) — the new mechanism for setting closing prices — has amplified volatility on weekly and monthly derivatives ‌expiry days since its introduction on August 3.

Brent crude rose 1.4% to $98.4 a barrel after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi forces said they attacked Saudi energy facilities.

Eight of the 16 major domestic sectors logged losses. Heavyweight financials and private banks slid 0.9% and ⁠1%, respectively.

Singed by the ‌pressure, the rupee declined to 94.8175 per dollar ‌by ⁠the end of the session, down 0.35% ⁠from its previous close.

Shriram General Insurance (SGI) today announced a strategic corporate agency partnership with SK Finance Limited, a 31-year-old leading NBFC in India. The partnership aims at expanding access to insurance solutions and increasing access to insurance protection for customers across key markets.

Through this partnership, SGI will offer its range of general insurance solutions through SK Finance’s 700+ branch network and other designated distribution channels. The association will enable customers to access relevant insurance solutions through SK Finance’s extensive distribution network, while the claims and servicing process will be handled by SGI through its established servicing and claims mechanisms.

Tata Consultancy Services has won a ₹ 122.6 crore bid to implement the next phase of the Odisha State Workflow Automation System (OSWAS 3.0), extending its partnership with the Odisha government by around 6 years.

Broader markets outperformed equity benchmarks. Sectorally, banking and financial stocks witnessed significant pressure, while defence and media outperformed.

Pranav Constructions’ ₹351-crore IPO has fetched 15.50 times subscription at 3.21 pm on the second day of bidding, with strong demand from non-institutional investors.

Alkem Laboratories Ltd has announced the launch of Renocia Exo, a next-generation hair regeneration therapy developed to support the health and vitality of the hair follicle through a comprehensive scientific approach. Shares traded at ₹5,186.50 on the NSE.

Top gainers: BEL (+1.57%), ONGC (+1.32%), HUL (+1.14%), Adani Ports (+1.04%), Eicher Motors (+0.73%)

Top losers: ICICI Bank (-1.98%), Axis Bank (-1.67%), SBI Life (-1.54%), Reliance (-1.43%), UltraTech (-1.23%)

Top gainers: GVT&D (+8.92%), Kalyan Jewellers (+4.16%), Laurus Labs (+3.58%), Bharat Forge (+3.05%)

Top losers: Blue Star (-2.41%), Hindustan Petroleum (-2.41%), 360 One WAM (-2.36%), Hitachi Energy (-2.27%)

HDFC Securities has announced that its global investing platform, available through InvestRight and HDFC SKY, has crossed 30,000 active investors, with nearly 2 lakh additional investors expressing interest in going global. The platform has also crossed $250 million in AUM, reflecting the growing appetite among Indian investors for international diversification. Notably, over 50% of investors are from Tier-II and Tier-III cities, highlighting how global investing is expanding beyond India’s metros.

Symphony shares zoomed 7% to ₹612.60 on the NSE. The company plans a phased India entry into air conditioners, BLDC ceiling fans and air purifiers from December 2026.

Shriram General Insurance (SGI) has announced a strategic corporate agency partnership with SK Finance Ltd, a 31-year-old leading NBFC in India. The partnership aims at expanding access to insurance solutions and increasing insurance protection for customers across key markets.

Chalet Hotels traded at ₹893.05 on the NSE, after opening higher at ₹907.35. The company has signed a share purchase agreement for the acquisition of 100% of the equity shares of Lakeview Mercantile Company Pvt Ltd.

Torrent Green Energy commissions 322 MWp solar projects in Maharashtra, supporting clean energy and agricultural sustainability under PM-KUSUM.

Ganesha Recycling Chain Private Ltd, a material subsidiary of Race Eco Chain, has approved the allotment of 93,379 0.01% compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares (CCPS) of face value of ₹10 each for an aggregate consideration of ₹4.66 crore to the company.

Jupiter Wagons Ltd, a provider of comprehensive mobility solutions encompassing rail, road and marine transportation, has secured a significant order from GATX India Private Ltd, a subsidiary of GATX Corporation, US, further strengthening its presence in India’s private wagon leasing ecosystem. Jupiter Wagons has signed a ₹97.66 crore (including applicable tax) wagon purchase agreement with GATX India Private Ltd. Shares were flat at ₹243.50 on the NSE.

OmniScience Capital expects India to benefit from rising FPI allocations; overweight on financial services, power and housing finance for the long term

According to OmniScience Capital, the recent shift in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows towards Indian equities could mark the beginning of a broader sentiment turnaround. Vikas Gupta, CEO and Chief Investment Strategist at OmniScience Capital, believes the consistent inflows seen in July and August could represent an initial move by global investors to diversify into non-AI assets.

Gupta said this could benefit India as global emerging-market allocations remain skewed towards Taiwan and South Korea, while India remains severely under-allocated despite being the fastest-growing major economy across emerging markets, Asia and the world.

S&P Global Ratings on Tuesday assigned 'BBB' long-term rating to Bank of India (BoI) on sufficient capitalisation, solid funding, and healthy liquidity.

Aluminium futures show a bullish trend, targeting ₹356, with strong support at ₹342 for potential gains.
